key_insight: Research agents propose worthwhile experiments, but evidence that their rankings improve which experiment to run remains limited.
engineering_relevance: Use research agents to generate candidate experiments, but validate their prioritization before relying on it to allocate compute or research effort.
method: Six frontier models, working alone or in teams, proposed, ranked and forecast minimum viable experiments for seven recent NLP papers.
A separate executor attempted all 415 experiments, including those ranked last.
Three model auditors assessed results; rankings and forecasts were compared with simple baselines.
evidence_signal: Of 415 experiments, 194 were judged sound, valuable and new, and 73 also beyond the seed paper and non-obvious; top choices beat random selection but did not demonstrably beat choosing the first-written experiment.
watch_item: Teams cost more without clear overall proposal-quality gains, and forecasts were not measurably better than those from fresh instances of the same models.
paper_title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
